scenes.text: Humans beamed a message at the stars that won't arrive for twenty five thousand years.
On November sixteenth, nineteen seventy four, it left the Arecibo telescope in Puerto Rico.
It was the grand finale of a ceremony for the dish's big upgrade.
Astronomer Frank Drake was in charge of building and sending it.
The message was one thousand six hundred seventy nine ones and zeros.
That number only splits into two primes, twenty three and seventy three.
Laid out in that grid, it draws numbers, the elements of life, and D N A.
Next to the D N A, it even counts about three billion base pairs.
Plus a human figure, our solar system, and the telescope itself.
Drake first tested it on his friend Carl Sagan, who cracked almost everything but the chemistry.
A one million watt transmitter fired it off in about three minutes.
Its target is M thirteen, a cluster of over three hundred thousand stars.
Some people say the cluster will have moved by the time the signal arrives.
Drake said it will only shift a fraction of the beam's width.
So our cosmic postcard is still on its way.
If aliens wrote back, what would you want them to say?

title: Humans sent a message to the stars in 1974 📡
caption: On Nov 16, 1974, the Arecibo telescope beamed 1,679 bits at star cluster M13. It arrives in about 25,000 years.
